title: Swahili Lamb Biriani
community: Swahili coast — Eid ul-Adha's most important dish
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Swahili Lamb Biriani — the grandest expression of the Swahili biryani tradition using lamb, the Eid sacrifice meat. Overnight-marinated lamb in yogurt and Zanzibar spices, layered with saffron rice and fried onions, sealed and dum-cooked. The most important food of the Tanzanian Islamic calendar.
longDesc: Lamb biryani for Eid ul-Adha is the Swahili coast's most important ceremonial food — the lamb sacrificed in the name of faith transformed by the island's greatest culinary technique into a dish of profound significance and extraordinary flavour. The dum cooking is performed with the same reverence as the sacrifice itself.
ingredients: 1.2 kg lamb — cubed, marinated overnight in yogurt-spice mix
½ tsp saffron in warm milk
// Marinade: 1 cup yogurt, 5 garlic, 2 tbsp ginger, 2 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp paprika, 2 tsp salt
steps: See TZA121 (Zanzibar Biryani) for the full technique — lamb biryani follows the same layering and dum cooking method.
Lamb requires 50—60 minutes pre-cooking to reach 90% doneness.
Seal tightly. Dum 30—35 minutes over lowest heat.
chefTips: See TZA121 for all detailed tips.
Lamb needs longer pre-cooking than chicken.
The rose water is the Eid signature.
cookingScience: See TZA121 for dum biryani cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Eid lamb from local Tanzanian pastoral communities.
culturalNote: Swahili lamb biryani for Eid ul-Adha is the most significant food the coast produces — the sacrifice made meaningful through the highest expression of the Swahili culinary tradition. To receive this biryani is to understand what the word 'celebration' means in Zanzibar.
